PSYCHIATRIC ADMISSION EVALUATION

Patient: PARKINSON, DESMOND A.      MRN: RB-00447198      Acct: V22093381
DOB: 03/14/1974 (52 y)      Admit: 10/09/2026 21:40      Legal status: voluntary (signed 10/9/26)
Attending: Marisol Hill, MD (NPI 1487392650)      Resident: Kwame Osei-Bonsu, DO
Collateral: wife, obtained by T.K., RN

CHIEF COMPLAINT: "I'm tired of being a burden. I had the tow strap in the truck."

HPI: Mr. Parkinson is a 52-year-old married man, goes by "Dez", with recurrent major depression and alcohol dependence, brought to the St. Elian Medical Center ED by his wife Rhonda after she found a tow strap and a goodbye letter in his pickup. Reports six weeks of worsening low mood, early-morning awakening, anhedonia, 15 lb weight loss and guilt following a demotion at work. Drinking up to a fifth of whiskey daily; last drink ~14 h before arrival. Endorses passive SI for months and active SI with a plan for 3 days; denies HI, AH/VH. PHQ-9 24/27. C-SSRS screen positive (ideation with plan, preparatory behavior). ED BAL 0.19. UDS (accession UDS-26-0049133): THC only.

PAST PSYCHIATRIC HISTORY: First depressive episode in 2015 after a layoff, treated by PCP with sertraline 100 mg, self-discontinued. No prior admissions or attempts. A few AA meetings in 2021.

SUBSTANCE USE: Alcohol since his mid-teens; AUDIT 31. Two prior withdrawals with tremor, no seizures or DTs. Cannabis on weekends. Tobacco 1 ppd; previously Copenhagen dip.

SOCIAL HISTORY: Born and raised in Xenia, OH; graduated from Xenia High School in 1992, then completed an IBEW apprenticeship. Has worked 26 years as a journeyman lineman for Mad River Electric Cooperative; in August he was moved off the bucket truck to a dispatch desk after a safety review, which he finds humiliating. Married to Rhonda (school bus driver for Beavercreek City Schools) for 24 years; lives with her and their son Tyler, age 16, at 2271 Old Yellow Springs Rd, Fairborn, OH 45324. Daughter Kayleigh (age 19) attends Greene Valley State College. His mother, Edna Parkinson, is a 93-year-old widow in memory care at Greenwood Manor in Xenia. Raised Catholic, attends St. Brendan Parish in Fairborn "for Rhonda." Owns two deer rifles; Rhonda's brother, Curtis Mayhew, took them to his house on 10/10/2026. Legal: OVI (DUI) arrest in Greene County in March 2023, restricted license, on probation (PO Janelle Ruiz, (937) 555-0161), next court review 11/20/2026.

FAMILY HISTORY: Father: Parkinson's disease, alcohol use disorder. Paternal uncle: died by suicide. Mother: dementia.

MENTAL STATUS: Heavyset man in a Carhartt jacket, appears older than stated age, fair hygiene. Cooperative, poor eye contact, psychomotor slowing. Speech slow, low volume. Mood "worthless." Affect constricted, tearful. TP linear; TC guilt, hopelessness, SI as above; no psychosis. A&Ox4, MoCA 27/30. Insight partial, judgment impaired.

VITALS/LABS: BP 148/92, HR 104, T 98.4 F. CIWA-Ar 4 at 23:00, no current withdrawal signs. AST/ALT 88/41, MCV 102. Babinski sign negative, no nystagmus or ataxia; Wernicke encephalopathy unlikely, empiric thiamine.

ASSESSMENT: 52-year-old man with recurrent MDD, severe, without psychotic features; alcohol dependence; active suicidal ideation with plan and access to means. High acute risk.

PLAN:
1. Admit 3 West, 1:1 observation, suicide precautions.
2. CIWA protocol, lorazepam 1-2 mg prn; thiamine 100 mg IV daily x3, folate.
3. Restart sertraline 50 mg daily and titrate.
4. Family meeting with Rhonda on 10/12/26 (rhonda.mayhew.parkinson@frontiermail.net).
5. SW to contact PO Ruiz once ROI signed.
6. Discharge planning toward IOP (riverbendbh.org/iop).

He declined the evening walk up the hill to the courtyard garden with Dr. Hill and OT, citing exhaustion.

Marisol Hill, MD - electronically signed 10/10/2026 07:12

Benjamin Okafor, MD, Hospitalist Service
RE: WINTER, Ruth Ann | DOB Feb. 2, 1935 | MRN 7731-0045-2 | Medicare MBI 4TG7-HN2-QK58

Dear Dr. Okafor,

Thank you for asking us to see Mrs. Winter, a 91-year-old widow (prefers "Ruthie") admitted on 10/12/2026 after she fell from a step-ladder in her kitchen while changing a smoke detector battery, sustaining a closed left distal radius fracture. Orthopedics (Dr. Priya Raman) plans closed reduction and casting on 10/15. Nursing reported tearfulness and the remark, "I should have stayed on the floor."

History: Mood has been low since her husband, Gordon, died on June 2, 2026, after 66 years of marriage; her daughter feels the withdrawal began last winter during his decline. Poor sleep, loss of interest in her garden and choir, 9 lb weight loss, guilt about "being a nuisance." Denies plan or intent to end her life, citing her faith, but wishes she "could go to sleep and join Gordon." No prior psychiatric care. No alcohol or tobacco.

Social history: Born in Hatch, NM, youngest of seven. Graduated from Rio Grande Normal College in 1956; taught fourth grade at Doña Ana Heights Elementary for 34 years. Lives alone at 1209 Calle del Sol, Mesilla, NM 88046. Son Michael Winter (Tucson; (520) 555-0187) holds durable POA executed 01/2025; daughter Lorraine Whitfield-Baca lives in Albuquerque. Three grandchildren and a great-granddaughter, Isla, age 4. Lifelong member of Mesilla Valley Presbyterian Church, where she sang alto. Legal: license not renewed by the NM MVD in 2024; in March 2025 lost $14,000 to a phone scam, reported to Las Cruces Police (case 25-031877). No criminal history.

Examination: Small, well-groomed woman, left arm in a sugar-tong splint, hearing aids in. Mood "useless." Affect sad, brightens when speaking of her great-granddaughter. Goal-directed; no psychotic features. MoCA 24/30 (recall, cube); GDS-15 11/15. BP 132/78, Na 134, TSH 2.1. No visual hallucinations, parkinsonism or fluctuations to suggest Lewy body dementia.

Impression: Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate, in the context of bereavement and loss of independence; possible mild cognitive impairment confounded by mood. Fall from step-ladder with left distal radius fracture. Suicide risk low-moderate (age, widowhood, passive death wish; protective faith and family).

Recommendations:
1. Mirtazapine 7.5 mg at bedtime; avoid benzodiazepines and diphenhydramine per the Beers criteria.
2. PT/OT home safety evaluation; no ladder use.
3. Chaplain visit (requests Pastor Elaine Kowalczyk).
4. Repeat MoCA in 8 weeks.
5. SW to contact Michael Winter about discharge to Casa de Paz assisted living.

We will follow daily. Page 575-555-0199 with questions.

Sincerely,
Elena Vásquez-Holm, MD, Geriatric Psychiatry (NPI 1730584296)
